title: I forgot my portal password. What should I do?
content: Use the official Forgot Password flow and follow verification instructions. If it fails, raise an IT ticket. Never share your password or OTP.

title: Campus Wi-Fi is not connecting. What information should I provide?
content: Try the official network instructions. If the issue continues, report the building/floor, device type, approximate time and error. Never include your password.

title: My assignment upload failed.
content: Check the LMS file requirements and connection. Keep a screenshot and report the course, assignment, time and error to IT. If a deadline is near, mention it.

title: My hall ticket is missing.
content: Check official exam notices and registration status. Raise an urgent Examinations Cell ticket with exam name, course and semester. Only authorized exam staff can confirm eligibility.

title: My result or marks look incorrect.
content: Check the official notice for review/revaluation deadlines. Raise an Examinations Cell ticket with subject code and exam session. Do not assume a review outcome.

title: Money was deducted but fees show unpaid.
content: Do not immediately pay again. Save date, amount and transaction reference, then contact Accounts through a secure ticket. Never send PINs, passwords or OTPs.

title: My attendance is incorrect.
content: Report the course code, class date and relevant evidence to the Academic Coordinator. AI cannot edit attendance; authorized staff must verify records.

title: How do I request a bonafide certificate?
content: Use the official student-services process if available, or raise a Certificate/Records ticket. The current college policy must confirm required documents and processing time.

title: My digital library access is not working.
content: Check your current student login and service availability. Raise a Library ticket with the service name and error; do not share your password.

title: How do I report a hostel maintenance issue?
content: Create a Hostel Maintenance ticket with block, floor and issue description. For immediate danger, contact campus security/emergency support directly too.

title: How do I report a bus timing issue?
content: Raise a Transport ticket with route/bus identifier, stop, date and approximate time. Use the latest official notice for schedules; AI must not invent timings.

title: Can I submit a confidential grievance?
content: Use the official confidential grievance flow. Access should be limited to authorized reviewers. Avoid sharing sensitive details in general chat; immediate danger requires urgent human/emergency help.

title: How do I raise a SmartDesk ticket?
content: Sign in, choose Create Ticket, select the closest category, describe the issue, add relevant details and optional evidence, review the suggested department, then confirm submission. Save the ticket ID.

title: How can I check my ticket status?
content: Open My Tickets and select the ticket to view status, assigned department and public updates. Internal notes are not shown to students.

title: What do ticket statuses mean?
content: OPEN is awaiting handling; IN_PROGRESS means staff are working; AWAITING_INFO means more details are needed; RESOLVED means a solution was recorded; CLOSED means completed; REJECTED means declined with a reason.

title: What is an SLA?
content: An SLA is a target for first response and resolution based on priority, not a guarantee. SmartDesk should display the deadline calculated from the active policy and escalate at-risk tickets.

title: Can AI create or assign tickets?
content: AI can draft a ticket and suggest category/department. Show the summary and obtain student confirmation before submission. Backend rules validate and record the actual action.

title: Can AI change my attendance, fees or exam results?
content: No. AI can explain procedures, but official records and ticket decisions require authorized staff or approved backend workflows.

title: AI grounding
content: Answer from approved, current, role-authorized sources. Cite source IDs. If evidence is missing or conflicting, say it cannot be verified and offer human help.

title: Ticket confirmation
content: AI may draft a ticket but must show category, department, priority and description and ask for confirmation before submission.

title: Routing
content: Use deterministic category-to-department rules. Model predictions are suggestions only. Low-confidence or sensitive cases require human review.

title: Authorization
content: Backend validates identity, current role, account status, ownership and department authorization. AI predictions never grant permissions.

title: Audit
content: Record actor, action, entity, timestamp, correlation ID and minimal metadata for privileged changes. Never log passwords, tokens or OTPs.

title: Privacy
content: Internal notes are never returned to students. Confidential grievances are restricted to authorized reviewers.

title: SLA
content: Demo targets are calendar-hour examples only. Production must define working hours, holidays, pause rules and escalation owners.

title: Official records
content: AI must not modify attendance, fee status, marks, eligibility or close tickets outside the approved backend workflow.

title: Files
content: Use private storage, validate file type/signature, enforce size/count limits and authorize every download.

title: Reopening
content: Demo rule: student may request reopening once within seven calendar days after RESOLVED; backend validates and logs request.
